title: Even and Odd Signal Decomposition
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Signals and Systems
Even Signals
Odd Signals
Signal Symmetry
description: Decompose a preset or hand-drawn signal x(t) into its even part x_e(t) = [x(t) + x(-t)]/2 and odd part x_o(t) = [x(t) - x(-t)]/2, read the worked calculation at a probe time, and verify that the two parts sum back to x(t).

learningObjectives: Explain even and odd symmetry in terms of reflection about t = 0
Apply the decomposition formulas to compute the even and odd parts of a signal at a given time
Verify that the even and odd parts sum to the original signal
Recognize the even and odd parts of pulses, triangles, sawtooth waves and one-sided exponentials
prerequisites: Time reversal and time shifting of signals

controls.label: Drag in the top plot to draw a custom signal

assumptions: Signals are sampled every 0.01 s on a grid that is symmetric about t = 0
A sample that falls on a jump takes the midpoint value

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked example with a movable probe point
keyQuestions: What happens to the odd part when a symmetric pulse is centered on t = 0?
Why do the even and odd parts of a signal that is zero for t < 0 carry equal energy?
Can a signal have two different even and odd decompositions?
commonMisconceptions: Every signal is either even or odd
The even part of a signal is the portion of the signal for t > 0
Shifting a signal in time does not change its even and odd parts
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the even and odd parts at a probe time by hand and compare with the calculation panel
Sketch the even and odd parts of e^(-t)u(t) before revealing them
